Brings **up to three GCE Electronics Eco-Devices 3 (ED3)** into Gladys
through their local HTTP API: their counters (teleinfo, consumption,
production, injection, storage, water, gas), the power of their current
clamps, the mains voltage, their two relays, the outputs of their X-8R
extensions and their X-THL sensors (temperature, humidity, luminosity).

> Readings checked against a real ED3: cce66's, a member of the Gladys
> forum (firmware 1.3.0), who recorded its answers; they are replayed in the
> tests: its MAC address (an invented one of the same form in the tests),
> its counters and the clamps and pulse inputs feeding them, the units of
> the teleinfo, clamp and water counters, the clamp power. The commands
> (relays R1 and R2) were not tested on a real device, and no X-8R nor
> X-THL extension has been seen on a real ED3 yet. Written from GCE's
> documentation of the ED3 API (Postman "API ED3", linked from the ED3) and
> cce66's free tools (ED3 Api-Deck and Mqtt-Deck). Tell us what you see on
> yours. Not affiliated with GCE Electronics.

## Setup

1. In the ED3, Configuration menu: set an **API key** and note it.
2. In Gladys, Integrations > Eco-Devices 3: type the address of the ED3
   (e.g. `192.168.1.60`, with `:port` only if you changed the port of its
   web server; give it a fixed address in your router) and the API key. On
   the same page, list in "Relays Gladys may drive" the relays Gladys must
   drive, and only those (`R1`, `R2`; see "Relays" below: never a pump, a
   ventilation, a door strike…). Then save.
3. "Test the connection" reads the ED3 at once (once an interval has passed
   since the last read) and shows what it found.
4. In Discover, create the devices you want. A listed relay comes as a
   switch (or a light); the others come **read only** ("State (read
   only)"): Gladys shows their state, nothing can switch them.

A relay listed **after** its creation stays read only until you click
**"Update"** on it in Discover: it then gets its switch (or light), next to
its "State (read only)", which stays. The status of the integration says how
many relays are read only while none is listed, and which listed relays
still wait for "Update".

The ED3 wants the API key in the address of every request, over plain http:
anyone who can watch your local network can read it, as with the ED3's own
page. The key is kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent
only to the ED3, and never written in the logs nor in the files of the
integration.

If the address answers as another GCE box (an IPX800 V5, an IPX800 V4 or an
Eco-Devices RT2), the status and "Test the connection" say so: no value is
published and no command is sent, not even a switch-off, and the switch-offs
kept are dropped. Use the integration of that box.

## What you get

| On the ED3                                 | In Gladys                                                    | Code (in the name) |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------ |
| Relays 1 and 2                             | read only, or a switch / light when you list it              | `R1`, `R2`         |
| Output of an X-8R                          | read only (state)                                            | `X8R4259840-3`     |
| Counter 0 (teleinfo total)                 | consumption index (kWh), counted by Gladys (energy and cost) | `C0`               |
| Counters 11 to 18 (consumption) (¹)        | consumption index (kWh), counted by Gladys (energy and cost) | `C11`              |
| Counters 20 and 21 (production) (¹)        | production index (kWh), counted by Gladys                    | `C20`              |
| Counter 19 (injection) (¹)                 | index of the energy fed into the grid (kWh), shown only      | `C19`              |
| Counters 1 to 10 (teleinfo tariffs)        | plain sensor "Tariff index (kWh)", never counted twice       | `C1`               |
| Counters 22 to 24 (storage) (¹)            | plain sensor "Storage index (kWh)"                           | `C22`              |
| Counters 25 to 27 (water), 28 and 29 (gas) | volume (m³), out of the energy monitoring                    | `C25`, `C28`       |
| Clamp linked to a counter                  | power (W), signed (²)                                        | `T1`               |
| Supply voltage                             | voltage (V)                                                  | `U`                |
| X-THL                                      | temperature (°C), humidity (%), luminosity (lux)             | `XTHL4325376`      |

The counter numbers are the ED3's (GCE assigns them by category). A counter
fed by a clamp or a pulse input is named after it in Discover, as the ED3
lists them (`ID_Logger_tore`, `ID_Logger_tore_neg`, `ID_Logger_pulse`,
`ToreName`, `PulseName`): "T1-EDF · Consumption (C11)", "T1-EDF (negative)
· Injection (C19)" for the counter of the clamp's other direction, "Eau ·
Water (C25)". The others take the name you gave the counter on the ED3
(read again every 10 minutes). A name changed later on the ED3 does not
rename a device already created. A counter at 0 (not set up, or not read by
the ED3 yet) is not offered; a clamp that feeds no counter (0 in both
lists) neither. The ED3 may list fewer than 30
counters (a real one listed 26): a counter is known by its ED3 id, never
by its place in the list, and one not listed is not offered.

Units: the teleinfo and clamp indexes are in Wh on the ED3, published in
kWh. Checked on a real one: its counter 0 (teleinfo) matched, within a few
minutes, the same Linky read by an Eco-Devices RT2; the counter of its
battery clamp grew at 56.7 W on average over 71 hours in Wh, while the
clamp read about 60 W at both readings (57 W on average at the first; 64 W
from its power and 59 W in the ED3's page data at the second): in mWh it
would be 0.06 W. That second reading came from address .161, the others
from .162 (the same ED3 by its indexes; asked). Water and gas in mL,
published in m³: compared with a real water meter (61,503.0 L on the
meter, 61,503,000 on the ED3). When the ED3 gives `ID_Logger_pulse` (the
counters its pulse inputs feed), an electricity counter fed by a pulse
input is not offered (its unit is not checked; the status names it), nor
one listed both by a clamp and by a pulse input. Without that list (absent:
an older firmware), which counters the pulse inputs feed is not known, and
such a counter is published in kWh as any other, its unit not checked.
When the ED3 gives that list in another form (another firmware), no
electricity counter that a clamp is not known to feed is offered, the
teleinfo (C0 to C10) included, and one already created in Gladys is no
longer updated while it lasts (the status names them). The counters 11 to 24 are not offered when a clamp is linked to a
counter outside 11 to 24 (see (¹)).

The ED3 is read every 15 seconds by default (10 s at least). A value the
ED3 does not give (absent, a text, out of range, a voltage of 0 V) is not
published: never as 0. An X-THL reporting a measurement fault (`ioFault`)
publishes nothing while it does, and the status names it. An X-8R or X-THL
without an extension code (an object created, nothing paired) is not
offered.

(¹) The counters a clamp may feed (11 to 24) are offered only when the ED3
lists its clamp links in the form a real one gives (`ID_Logger_tore`: 8
entries, each 0 or a counter id; `ID_Logger_tore_neg` the same when given):
that is how their unit (Wh) was checked. An ED3 that does not give that
list, or gives it in another form (another firmware), does not say which
counters its clamps feed: counters 11 to 24 are then held, and the status
names those holding an index ("C11, C19 not offered: this ED3 does not list
the counters its clamps feed in the expected form…"). Nothing is guessed
from a list of another form.

(²) The clamp power is the ED3's `puissance` (mW, published in W, one
decimal): on a real ED3 it equals current × voltage × power factor for each
clamp (1,455,467 mW for 6.58 A × 235.5 V × 0.94). Its sign is kept: positive
in the direction of the clamp's `ID_Logger_tore` counter, negative in that
of its `ID_Logger_tore_neg` counter. Which direction is consumption or
production depends on how the clamp is set up on the ED3: the counter's
number and name say it (on a real ED3, a solar clamp produces in the
positive direction, towards its production counter C20, and three other
clamps have their negative direction towards consumption counters). A
clamp listed for one direction only still shows the other one, as a power
counted by no counter.

## Counters: lifetime indexes, never 0, a drop or a jump held

The index of a counter is a lifetime meter: Gladys derives the consumption
(and its cost) and the production from it; the injection index is shown,
Gladys computes nothing from it. The integration passes it through a guard:

- an index of 0 is never sent;
- an index that drops, or rises more than a home can draw (100 kW of
  electricity, 10 m³/h of water, 16 m³/h of gas, plus a small slack), is
  **held back**: the last accepted value is sent again, the status says it
  ("Index held back: C11 (↑ 4072.301 → 14072.301 kWh)"), and it stays held
  across a restart. Neither time nor repetition makes it accepted;
- only if it is right (an index reset on the ED3), click **"Accept the held
  index" twice**. **Gladys counts an accepted jump in full, at once**
  (consumption and cost); an accepted drop is published and nothing is
  counted for it. After "Attach the devices" to another ED3 whose index is
  higher, do not accept: delete the counter device and create it again (its
  history starts over). The first click lists the held values
  and takes nothing; the second, 3 seconds to 5 minutes later, takes exactly
  those values (plus what the meter may measure between the clicks), for
  each counter whose held value has not changed otherwise. Saving the
  configuration never accepts;
- the state of the guard is written to `/data` **before** Gladys gets the
  index: if `/data` cannot be written or read (or does not answer within
  5 s), no index is sent, and the status says so;
- an index is sent once a minute at most.

The guard counts time on the session clock (the wall clock at start, then
the time elapsed): a system clock that jumps does not widen its margin. A
counter device deleted and created again starts from the value Gladys keeps
for it.

## Relays: read only unless you list them

A relay you do not list is **read only**. To drive one from Gladys, list it
in "Relays Gladys may drive", e.g. `R1, R2:light` (`:light` makes it a
light, a switch otherwise), preferably before creating it in Discover;
already created, click "Update" on it in Discover. A switch or a light
obeys every "turn everything off" of Google, Alexa, the MCP and the scenes:
never list a pump, a freezer, a ventilation, a heating, a door strike nor a
valve. Only R1 and R2 can be listed: the X-8R outputs stay read only in this
version. A relay removed from the list is read only again at once: its
commands are refused, and a switch-off the integration still held for it is
dropped (in memory and in `/data`, after a restart too). Its switch stays on
the device in Gladys (without effect): Gladys does not delete a single
feature.

The commands go through `GET /api/object/ed3/0/SetOnR/<n>` and
`SetOffR/<n>` (absolute: never a toggle).

### Switching a listed relay off goes before anything

Switching off a listed relay needs no option and goes before everything
else: during a pause after failed reads, with a refused API key, with the
command queue full, and before the first read after a restart. Clicked, it
cuts any request in flight (a read, a read back, a command, a resend), but
another switch-off clicked just before (cut in its turn once it has gone
1 s without an answer).

It is refused only when: the address or the API key is missing; the relay
is not listed, or is not R1 or R2; the value is not 0 or 1; the ED3 read is
proven to be another one (another MAC address, see "Each ED3 keeps its
devices"); the address answers as another GCE box; the slot holds the same
ED3 as an earlier slot (see "Several ED3"). Clicked before the configuration is read from Gladys (the API key
lives there only, never in `/data`), it asks Gladys for it at once and waits
3 s; if it has not come, it is kept in memory and sent as soon as the key is
known, before anything goes to Gladys; if the relay turns out not to be
listed, the status says so. When the ED3 does not take it within 3.5 s (no
connection), it is kept (in `/data`) and sent again as soon as the ED3 is
free, before the read backs, by the next reads that show the relay on, and
after a restart.

A switch-off the reads do not show is sent again, 3 times at most; then the
status says so (check on site). It stays held until a newer command on that
relay leaves (your click), or, once applied, another state read twice in a
row (changed on the ED3 itself, by its scenarios or its page): never by the
time. A switch-on asked before the switch-off and not sent yet is cancelled:
nothing leaves after it. A switch-on sent before the switch-off and left
without an answer, if the ED3 still applies it within 5 s of its leaving, is
no change on the ED3: the switch-off is sent again.

## Commands

A command is written within 3.5 s of the click or refused with "nothing was
sent". It is then read back on the ED3: the value asked is a success; the
state before is "not applied yet"; no answer in time gives "sent, without
confirmation". Two reads follow, 5 s and 20 s later. The commands of a scene
are written one after the other, then read back once. One request at a time
to the ED3.

## Several ED3

Keep the first one in the top fields, and put the second one in
**"Eco-Devices 3 #2"** (address, API key, its drivable relays), a third one
in "Eco-Devices 3 #3". Each has its own devices in Discover ("ED3 #2 ·
Relay 1 (R1)"), its list of drivable relays and its status on its line. The
poll interval and the language are shared; "Accept the held index" applies
to all.

**Do not change the slot of an ED3 to try another one**: the devices
already created stay with their slot.

**An ED3 goes in one slot only**: its counters would be counted twice. A
slot with the address of an earlier slot is not read; a slot that reads the
same ED3 as an earlier slot (same MAC address, its IP here and its name
there, say) is not used, read again every 5 minutes only. Either way,
nothing is published for it, no command leaves from it (not even a
switch-off: the devices of the earlier slot drive that same ED3), and the
status says so. So that the same ED3 is told before anything is offered, a
slot after the first reads its ED3, at each start, once the earlier slots
have read theirs (or failed, or read nothing: no address, a refused key, a
pause): 25 seconds at most, once per start.

## Each ED3 keeps its devices

A device created for an ED3 never gets the values of another ED3 nor drives
its relays, even if you change the address of its slot (but the limit below, without a MAC address). The integration
keeps, in `/data`, which ED3 the devices of each slot belong to:

- by its **MAC address** when `GET /api/system/info` gives one (read again
  every round, kept as a salted fingerprint, never in clear);
- otherwise by its **address and port**. **Limit**: GCE does not document
  the MAC address (a real ED3, firmware 1.3.0, gives it as `macAdress`,
  `XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX`); an ED3 that gives none is not told apart from
  another one put at the same address, and a change of address needs
  "Attach the devices".

If the ED3 read is not theirs: no command leaves for it, not even a
switch-off; the switch-offs kept for the old one are dropped; none of its
values is published onto these devices; Discover is empty for that slot;
the status says so.

Then put back the address of their ED3. If you **replaced** it (or it moved
to another address without a readable MAC), click **"Attach the devices"
twice** (within a minute), choosing the slot: its values then go to these
devices and its listed relays obey them. The indexes stay guarded: a new
ED3 whose counters differ sees its indexes held until you accept them. A
slot without any device created simply takes the ED3 it reads.

When the MAC address of an ED3 that gave one cannot be read, only
switch-offs leave, and only to the address it was last checked at; if it
stays unreadable, "Attach the devices" (two clicks) attaches it by its
address: the first MAC address read afterwards becomes its identity, without
being compared (you chose it by its address). At
start, and after a failed read, its MAC address is read again before
anything is sent: the switch-offs kept leave after that check, and a
switch-off clicked waits for it 1.5 s at most, then leaves for the address
it was last checked at.

If `/data` is empty while devices exist (deleted, or an installation
restored on another machine: the Gladys Plus backup does not hold the data
of the integrations), or cannot be read, which ED3 the devices belong to is
unknown. Nothing proves it is another one: switch-offs leave, to the address
typed; switching on and the values stay refused until "Attach the devices"
(two clicks), and the status says so. While `/data` can be neither read nor
written, "Attach the devices" is refused too (it would not be kept). A read or a write
of `/data` that does not answer within 5 s counts as a failure: it holds
neither the reads nor the commands.

## Pauses and refusals

A failed read pauses 10 s, 30 s, 1 min, 2 min then 5 min (a minute at least
when the ED3 answers 429 or 503), the pause kept across a restart; switching
a relay on is refused until the pause ends. An API key refused by the ED3
(401, 403 on its main read) stops the reads until you change the key or
"Test the connection" succeeds. A secondary read that fails (counters,
names, X-8R, X-THL, `system/info`), even with a 401, stops nothing: what it
gave stays known, without value, and the status says so. While an ED3
cannot be read (or refuses the key), its devices leave Discover; a Scan does not
bring them back. They come back with the first read that succeeds.

## Limits

- Relays R1 and R2, counters, clamps, voltage, X-8R (read only) and X-THL;
  not the detailed teleinfo frame (apparent power, current tariff), the
  states of the pulse inputs themselves (the counters they feed are read),
  the X-8R commands, the schedules, the virtual variables nor
  Modbus in this version.
- The clamp power is one signed value (W): Gladys gets no separate
  production feature; the counters of each direction carry the energy.
- The integration reads the local HTTP API, not the MQTT of the ED3.
- Three ED3 at most per integration.
- http only (the ED3 answers over http on the local network).

## How to install Eco-Devices 3 in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Eco-Devices 3 appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-ecodevices-ed3:0.2.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-ecodevices-ed3](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-ecodevices-ed3).

Eco-Devices 3 requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Eco-Devices 3 is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), not by the Gladys core team.

- [Browse all integrations](/docs/integrations/), native and community
- [Build and publish your own external integration](/docs/dev/external-integrations/)
- [Source code on GitHub](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-ecodevices-ed3) — [source of this documentation](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-ecodevices-ed3/blob/HEAD/docs/en.md)
